title: AWS Taps Qualcomm: A Strategic Play for Next-Gen AI and Hyperscale Networking
summary: Amazon Web Services is partnering with mobile chip titan Qualcomm in a multi-generational effort to develop custom silicon. These specialized chips will power AI inference workloads and ultra-fast 1.6 Tbps optical networking within AWS's data centers, solidifying its vertical integration strategy.
content:
In a move poised to reshape the future of cloud infrastructure, Amazon Web Services (AWS) has thrown its formidable weight behind mobile chip giant Qualcomm, announcing a multi-generational collaboration to develop bespoke silicon.

This isn't just a handshake; it's a deep dive into creating custom chips specifically tailored for AI inference workloads and incredibly fast 1.6 terabit-per-second (Tbps) optical networking gear. This partnership aims to integrate these critical components directly into AWS’s sprawling data centers, optimizing performance and efficiency from the ground up.

For AWS, this collaboration signifies a continued drive towards vertical integration and optimized performance. The cloud titan has consistently invested in its own custom silicon, from Graviton processors to Inferentia and Trainium AI accelerators, aiming to offer superior performance-per-watt and cost efficiency tailored precisely to its colossal operations. This new venture with Qualcomm extends that strategy into even more specialized domains.

For Qualcomm, traditionally a powerhouse in mobile computing, this represents a significant legitimization of its ambitions within the datacenter arena. While they’ve been making inroads, a direct, multi-year engagement with the world's largest cloud provider is a game-changer, demonstrating immense confidence in their design prowess beyond smartphones and consumer devices.

The focus on AI inference chips is particularly telling. As AI adoption explodes, the demand for efficient, high-performance inference at scale is paramount. Coupling this with bleeding-edge 1.6 Tbps optical networking infrastructure underscores AWS's commitment to building a future-proof backbone capable of handling the unprecedented data flows required by tomorrow's AI-driven applications and services.

While initial announcements might lean on industry buzzwords, the implications of such a strategic alliance are profound, promising to deliver optimized, custom hardware that could redefine the benchmarks for cloud-based AI and networking performance for years to come.
keyTakeaways: AWS is deepening its commitment to custom silicon, diversifying its supply chain for critical AI and networking components.
Qualcomm gains a significant foothold and validation in the hyperscale datacenter market through this multi-generational partnership.
The collaboration targets high-performance AI inference and cutting-edge 1.6 Tbps optical networking, essential for future cloud infrastructure demands.
author: Tobias Mann

title: Cybersecurity Gets Smarter: Tenable Taps Anthropic's Claude Mythos 5 for Next-Gen Threat Prediction
summary: Tenable is integrating Anthropic's advanced AI, Claude Mythos 5, into its Tenable One platform to power a new "Adversary View." This move aims to equip enterprise security teams with cutting-edge adversarial reasoning, allowing them to proactively anticipate and defend against potential cyber breaches.
content:
Cybersecurity has always been a high-stakes game of cat and mouse, but the mouse just got a whole lot smarter. Tenable, a key player in exposure management, is making a significant leap forward by integrating Anthropic’s frontier AI model, Claude Mythos 5, directly into its Tenable One platform. This isn't just another feature; it's a fundamental shift, powering a new "Adversary View" designed to anticipate how attackers might breach an organization's digital walls.

Imagine having a crystal ball that predicts a hacker's next move before they even make it. That's the promise of Tenable's latest innovation. By harnessing Claude Mythos 5’s sophisticated adversarial reasoning, the Tenable One platform can now model complex attack paths with unprecedented depth. It’s about moving beyond simply identifying vulnerabilities to truly understanding how a determined adversary would chain them together, exploit them, and ultimately compromise an environment. This capability provides a proactive edge, enabling security teams to patch not just individual holes, but entire attack routes.

The inclusion of Claude Mythos 5 signals a new era for enterprise security, where advanced AI isn't just analyzing logs but actively thinking like an attacker. This allows Tenable One to generate highly accurate, actionable insights into potential breach scenarios. For stretched security operations centers, this means a dramatic improvement in prioritization, focusing resources where they matter most and preempting threats that might otherwise slip through the cracks. It's about turning hypothetical risks into concrete, preventable actions, fundamentally changing the defensive playbook.

This strategic integration positions Tenable at the forefront of AI-driven cybersecurity. As the digital threat landscape continues to evolve with alarming speed and complexity, leveraging AI to gain a predictive advantage isn't just beneficial—it's becoming essential. The "Adversary View" powered by Claude Mythos 5 could very well set a new industry standard for how enterprises manage their cyber risk and stay one step ahead of the bad actors.
keyTakeaways: Tenable is integrating Anthropic's advanced Claude Mythos 5 AI into its Tenable One exposure management platform.
This integration powers a new "Adversary View" feature, designed to provide frontier adversarial reasoning.
The new capabilities will help enterprise customers proactively anticipate potential cyberattack paths and strengthen their defenses.
author: Eric Doerr

title: SMA Devices Get a Pythonic Upgrade: New sma-modbus Library Hits PyPI
summary: A new asynchronous Python library, `sma-modbus`, has landed on PyPI, offering developers an open-source tool to interface with SMA energy devices via Modbus TCP. While currently in developer preview, this release promises enhanced control and integration for smart energy systems once production-ready.
content:
The world of smart energy management just got a significant boost for Python developers. A brand-new asynchronous Python library, aptly named `sma-modbus`, has officially debuted on PyPI, opening up a direct and streamlined channel to interface with SMA devices via Modbus TCP. This arrival marks a notable step forward for those looking to integrate or automate their SMA-powered energy systems using one of the most popular programming languages.

Built upon the reliable `modbus-connection` foundation, `sma-modbus` provides a robust, async framework, allowing developers to communicate with SMA inverters, battery storage systems, and other smart energy components with efficiency and responsiveness. For anyone building custom monitoring dashboards, home automation scripts, or advanced energy management applications, this library offers the much-needed programmatic access to real-time data and control capabilities that were previously more cumbersome to achieve. Its asynchronous nature means applications can interact with devices without blocking, leading to more fluid and performant solutions.

However, enthusiasts eager to dive in should heed a crucial note: `sma-modbus` is currently labeled as a "Developer Preview." This means while functional and actively developed, the creators explicitly caution against its use in mission-critical production environments just yet. This pre-release status is a testament to the collaborative heart of the open-source movement, inviting the broader developer community to test, experiment, and contribute by diligently reporting any issues they encounter. Their feedback is not just welcome, it’s invaluable in refining the library and hardening it for eventual stable releases. This collective effort ensures that when `sma-modbus` finally sheds its preview tag, it will emerge as a truly robust and reliable tool, empowering a new generation of smart energy applications.
keyTakeaways: `sma-modbus` is a new asynchronous Python library now available on PyPI.
It enables programmatic interaction with SMA energy devices using the Modbus TCP interface, built on `modbus-connection`.
The library is currently a "Developer Preview," functional but not recommended for production, with developers seeking community feedback.
